title: Max the Reading Buddy
author: Shellfie original
credit: An original story written for the McKinley Bulldogs.

pages: Every Friday, Max's third grade class visits a kindergarten class for Reading Buddies. Each big kid is paired with a little kid, and they read together for half an hour. Max's buddy is Nico, who is five, has a gap where his front tooth used to be, and is very worried about reading. "I can't read big words," Nico says the first day. "I can only read cat."

Max remembers being five. Reading felt like trying to open a jar that was screwed on too tight. So Max picks an easy book about a frog and lets Nico choose where to sit. They squeeze into the reading corner on a beanbag, and Max says, "Let's read it together. You point to the words, and I'll help when you need me."

Nico points to the first word and stops. It is "frog." Max wants to just say it, but Max remembers what good reading helpers do: wait first. Max counts to three silently. Nico whispers, "F... f-r... frog!" "You figured it out yourself!" Max says. Nico's whole face lights up.

When Nico gets stuck on a hard word, Max gives a hint instead of the answer. "Look at the first letter. What sound does it make?" When Nico reads a page all the way through, Max gives him a high five. When Nico makes a mistake and fixes it, Max says, "Great fix! That's what real readers do."

Week by week, Nico reads more pages and asks for help less. In December, the buddies trade books in a book exchange. Nico gives Max a book about sharks with a note inside, written in big wobbly letters: "MAX IS MY BUDY." Max doesn't fix the spelling. Max tapes the note inside the cover and decides it is the best book Max owns.

quiz.q: What did Nico write in the note?
Why did Max wait before saying the word "frog"?
o: To give Nico a chance to figure it out
Because Max didn't know the word
